subject: Haze in its element, concept A (a lavender field at dusk) against concept B (layered hills at blue hour)
prompt: critic/ab/PROMPT-DUEL.txt, its second paragraph worded for two candidate pictures of the same page

judges.notes: Prefers B: the violet horn reads as tinted cast acrylic with crisp rims; one tint across horn and cabinet; a brighter, readable cabinet against gold grass; right-third layout with copy space; layered haze depth. A wins: the lavender and path read as photography; base visible with a contact line; sun clear of the product. B: grass reads as CG hair, base hidden in it, the sun disc touches the horn's top.

Prefers A: the whole cabinet, ports and a contact line on the soil path; copper rim light and the lavender bent through the clear side; rows lead to a centred product; backlit lavender reads photographic. But A's horn is blown to milky pink (R 255 over ~80% of its right half) and its lower corners sink near black (median ~37). B: a rich violet horn and a light pastel range with room for a headline; but the throat a smoky smear, base and ports hidden in hair-like grass, flat foggy front light (the cabinet as matte painted panels), the sun disc on the horn's top edge in line with the far ridge.

Prefers B: the horn deep violet tinted acrylic with refraction through the flare; the product on the right third, the left half and top clean for copy; evenly exposed. A: the horn clipped (R 255 over ~70%, ~37 levels), a pale-pink pillow round a black throat, off the cabinet's tint; dead centre, so a spread's gutter runs through it; the front in its own shadow (~47); the lavender breaks into crossed leaf cards where it meets the path. A wins: the side panel's transparency, the full base and contact, a low backlight and depth. B: base buried in wiry grass; a uniform low-contrast haze; the sun disc on the horn's top edge.

agreed: All three faulted A's horn, blown to pale pink in the backlight, and B's base, hidden in hair-like grass with the hazy sun sitting on the horn's top edge.
